title: Proof of qbeta canonical markov weights explicit instance
html:
Proof. Proof of qbeta canonical markov weights explicit instance

Proof of the normalisation axiom

y_{(3)}(q) + 2 \, y_{(2,1)}(q) + y_{(1,1,1)}(q)
= z(q) + 2 \left( \tfrac{1}{2} - z(q) \right) + z(q)
= 1

This holds for every q > 0. The Lean discharge is ring. \square

Scope of the instance

This explicitly constructs an instance of CanonicalMarkovWeightsH3. It establishes that:

  • The class CanonicalMarkovWeightsH3 has at least one inhabitant.
  • All conditional theorems stated under [CanonicalMarkovWeightsH3] (specifically delta_tau_M_canonical_has_q2_minus_1_factor and its corollary delta_tau_M_canonical_vanish_at_one_via_factor) are not vacuous.
  • The class formalism naturally accommodates the archimedean \sqrt q structure expected from the canonical Wenzl–Markov construction.

It does not establish:

  • That this instance is the canonical Wenzl–Markov weights. The canonical weights from H_3(q) have a specific closed form derived from the Hecke algebra's Bratteli diagram and quantum dimensions. They are tied to the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \cdot \sigma_{n-1}) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_{n-1}(q). Identifying the canonical inhabitant remains open. CLOSED 2026-09-03 — see below.
  • A formula for \Delta\mathrm{tr}_M^{\text{can}}(q) at this instance, though it is computable via delta_tau_M_canonical_has_q2_minus_1_factor.
  • Any bearing on the c_k ladder closure.

The canonical inhabitant, identified

QOU.BraidKnot.CanonicalMarkovWeightsH3.canonicalInstance, sorry-free, carries the production trace's own weights:

  y_{(3)} = \frac{[4]_q}{[2]_q^{3}} = \frac{q^4+1}{(q^2+1)^2},
  \qquad
  y_{(2,1)} = \frac{1}{[2]_q^{2}} = \frac{q^2}{(q^2+1)^2},
  \qquad
  y_{(1^3)} = 0 .

These are exactly the convention-D values this block already quotes below; what was missing was the Lean instance, not the mathematics.

Why they are the canonical ones, rather than merely another inhabitant. Convention D is the N=2 member of the Ocneanu family z_N = q^N/[N]_q — its framing ratio a^2 = z/z_- is the monomial q^4, which collapses every Ocneanu numerator into quantum integers and turns the weight product into the hook-content formula w_\lambda = \dim_q(V_\lambda^{\mathfrak{sl}_N})/[N]_q^{\,n} (see rem:markov-z-reconciliation). So the three values are derived from the trace, not chosen to satisfy the class axiom — and the vanishing y_{(1^3)} = 0 is the \mathfrak{sl}_2 row bound, since a partition with more than N rows has a cell of content -N whose numerator factor carries [0]_q = 0.

Derived, not merely checked (2026-09-03). The three values are proved equal to the n = 3 Markov weights that QOU.SchurWeyl.HeckeMarkov3 solves from tr_M(1) = 1, tr_M(\sigma_1) = z and the Markov relation — canonical_y3_eq_markovWeight0, canonical_y21_eq_markovWeight2, markovWeight1_at_markovZD in QOU.BraidKnot.QBetaCanonicalMarkovWeightsDerived — and hence to the n = 3 slice of the general-n ocneanuWeight at z_D (canonicalInstance_eq_ocneanuWeight). The family and the hook-content identification invoked in the previous paragraph are prior art in Lean (WenzlWeightVanishing, SchurWeyl/OcneanuWeight*, WenzlWeightLevelR; PRs #5242, #5575), credited late — see the note in rem:markov-z-reconciliation.

The normalisation is an identity, not a constraint that had to be arranged. The class axiom y_{(3)} + 2y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)} = 1 reduces to (q^4+1) + 2q^2 = (q^2+1)^2, which holds for every q with no positivity hypothesis — equivalently [4]_q = ([2]_q^2 - 2)[2]_q, so [4]_q/[2]_q^3 = 1 - 2/[2]_q^2.

The pre-existing explicitInstance is untouched and was never wrong. It satisfies the class axiom because z + 2(\tfrac12 - z) + z = 1 for any z — which is precisely why it inhabits the class without being the production weights. It differs from the canonical set on all three blocks.

It is now the class's default instance (owner decision, 2026-09-03, bean qou-6u92), so a bare delta_tau_M_canonical q means the production trace's \Delta\tau_M rather than the \sqrt q-bearing toy.

The promotion was made as a pair with demoting explicitInstance from instance to def, and the pairing is the point: two global instances of one class is a silent hazard, since resolution takes the later declaration and nothing in the source says so. With exactly one instance, what a bare use means is stated rather than inferred. explicitInstance remains a first-class inhabitant and every use of it is unchanged — they all name it explicitly with @ — it is simply no longer a candidate for implicit resolution.

The change is machine-guarded, not asserted: delta_tau_M_canonical_resolves_to_canonical is rfl-provable only because resolution picks the canonical weights, so declaring a second instance or promoting explicitInstance back would stop it typechecking rather than silently changing what every bare use means. The guard was verified to have teeth — the same statement written against explicitInstance does not typecheck. All five files that mention the class are lean-direct exit 0, against a green baseline taken before the change.

Measurement: canonical_markov_weights_h3_are_sl2_dimensions.py (11/11).

Numerical sanity check

At the substrate parameter q = q_0 \approx 1.10998, this instance's own parameter is z(q_0) = \sqrt{q_0} / (1 + q_0) \approx 0.499. Note that this is 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}), the excised convention C value, not the framework's production z = q^3/(q^2+1) \approx 0.6127; the instance is a formal inhabitant of the class and is free to carry it, but the symbol z here does not mean what it means elsewhere in the paper. The value is close to 1/2 by accident, since \sqrt{q_0} \approx 1.054 and (1 + q_0)/2 \approx 1.055. This instance gives y_{(3)}(q_0) \approx 0.499, y_{(2,1)}(q_0) \approx 0.001, and y_{(1,1,1)}(q_0) \approx 0.499. The sum is 0.499 + 2(0.001) + 0.499 = 1.000, satisfying normalisation.

The canonical Wenzl weights at q_0 are y_{(3)} = [4]_q/[2]_q^3 \approx 0.5054042, y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_q^2 \approx 0.2472979, and y_{(1^3)} = 0 exactly — convention D, the production trace. They satisfy the normalisation \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1 exactly, with d = (1, 2, 1); there is no truncation residue. The values (0.4154,\ 0.2809,\ 0.0227) previously called canonical here, and attributed to markov_weights_symbolic.solve_y_lambda(3), are convention C, excised by the owner ruling of 2026-08-09, and their reported sum 0.9999 was a truncation artefact of that same excised route. Check the convention of any markov_weights_symbolic call against the trace-convention registry before quoting it again.

The mismatch between this instance and the canonical weights survives the convention change, but it moves. On the (3) block the gap shrinks: the instance gives y_{(3)} = z(q_0) \approx 0.4993 against the canonical \approx 0.5054, a \approx 1.2\,\% discrepancy where against the excised C value 0.4154 it was \approx 20\,\%. What now decides it outright is the rest of the vector: the instance has y_{(2,1)} \approx 0.0007 against the canonical \approx 0.2473, and y_{(1,1,1)} \approx 0.4993 where the canonical value is 0 exactly. So this is still not the canonical instance, but the sharpest evidence is the vanishing of the (1^3) block, not the size of the (3) block. The class admits infinitely many inhabitants, and this construction merely identifies one.
